beats.text: Welcome to episode four. So far we've treated fuels as equations. Today we look at the fuels themselves: where they come from, how biofuels are made, and what the carbon in them does over time.

First, two quick checks from last episode. Does a catalyst change the delta H of a reaction? And if two moles of hydrogen burning has delta H equal to negative five hundred and seventy-two kilojoules, what is the molar enthalpy of combustion of hydrogen? Pause and answer.

A catalyst lowers the activation energy but does not change delta H. And the molar enthalpy of combustion of hydrogen is negative two hundred and eighty-six kilojoules per mole of hydrogen: half the value, because the equation was for two moles.
